published.note: Year only; exact publication day not sourced in this session.

summary.plain: UA2 reported the observation of eight events interpreted as the Z0 boson decaying into an electron and a positron (sometimes with a photon). Four of them gave a Z mass of 91.9 ± 1.3 (stat) ± 1.4 (syst) GeV/c². The paper's title says 'Evidence for Z0 → e+e−'.
summary.technical: UA2 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 129 (1983) 130: from a search for electron pairs in p-pbar collisions at sqrt(s) = 550 GeV, eight events interpreted as p-pbar -> Z0 + anything with Z0 -> e+e- or e+e-γ, where Z0 is the neutral Intermediate Vector Boson postulated by the unified electroweak theory; four of the events are used to measure Mz = 91.9 ± 1.3 (stat) ± 1.4 (syst) GeV/c². Received 11 August 1983; issue dated 15 September 1983.

title: Evidence for Z0 -> e+ e- at the CERN anti-p p Collider
why_it_matters: A second CERN collider experiment's measurement of the Z0 mass from four of its eight Z0 → e+e− candidate events, 91.9 ± 1.3 (stat) ± 1.4 (syst) GeV/c², published in the same year as UA1's Z paper.
